mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of quarters with 2%+ GDPC1 growth, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be negative over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs reduce economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.035 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3pp increase in UNRATE over 3 months indicates labor market softening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary easing.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances with rising UNRATE, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.025 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between INDPRO and HOUST: when industrial production (INDPRO) grows by 1.5% while housing starts (HOUST) decline by 5% over 2 months, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be negative over the next 20 trading days due to supply chain imbalances.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 45% of instances with specified proxy interaction, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on signal: RSAFS (retail sales) consistently predicts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with higher sales indicating positive returns due to strong consumer demand.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns do not significantly correlate with RSAFS growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Regime-conditional: in a monetary easing cycle, a 1% decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation rate) over 2 months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as reduced inflation expectations support equity valuations.
regime_hint: monetary easing cycle with low inflation
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of easing cycle instances with declining CPIAUCSL, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between PAYEMS (non-farm payrolls) and UNRATE: when payrolls grow by 200,000 while UNRATE remains below 4.5% over 1 month, S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be positive over the next 20 trading days due to a strong labor market with controlled unemployment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances with specified proxy interaction, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Threshold-triggered signal: when INDPRO exceeds 105 (indicating strong industrial production growth), S&P 500 forward returns are likely to be positive over the next 5 trading days as supply chains efficiently meet demand.
failure_condition: SPX fails to produce positive 5-day returns in > 55% of instances with INDPRO > 105, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.025 over any 1.5-year rolling window.
